steps.path: Voice → Your words, a long list
steps.headline: A long word list now fades at the edge where more is hidden.
steps.changed: The last visible row fades out instead of being cut off flat.
steps.notice: Same fade as every popup's body — now one fade everywhere.

steps.path: Pages screen, the list on the left
steps.headline: The Pages list fades at its bottom edge when it scrolls.
steps.changed: "Release board" fades out under the list instead of being cut off.
steps.notice: Same on the Office home, games, first-run setup and about 60 other places.

steps.headline: Popups: one fade, appearing instantly.
steps.changed: The old painted band over the edge is replaced by the content fading, the same look as everywhere else; it no longer eases in.
steps.notice: Settings, Resume, the file viewer and project popups also lose an unfaded strip at each side.

steps.headline: Resume: the same one fade.
steps.changed: Its own private fade is replaced by the shared one.

steps.path: The sessions list from the top bar
steps.headline: The sessions menu: the fade now actually shows.
steps.changed: These lists had the fade's name but never switched it on; now they fade.

steps.path: The model chip in the status bar
steps.headline: The model picker's list fades in every style.
steps.changed: The fuller style of the picker had no fade; now it matches the flat one.

steps.path: The chat transcript, conversation preview, Marketplace and Library pages
steps.headline: Should the chat and the Marketplace/Library pages get a fade too, using a faded copy of the wallpaper?
steps.today: These four are the only scrolling areas left without a fade. A normal fade there stops the frosted cards and bubbles from blurring the wallpaper behind them.
steps.problem: They break the new "every scroll area fades" rule, and the chat transcript is the most-seen scroll area in the app.

options.label: Build the wallpaper fade
pros: Every scroll area in the app fades, no exceptions.
The Minimalist layout's chat already does this, so the look exists.
cons: More work, and a full-screen effect that has to be checked in every theme.

options.label: Keep them as exceptions
pros: No risk to the frosted look; the branch closes sooner — why I recommend it for now.
The exceptions are written down and guarded.
cons: Four places still scroll without a fade.
